title: The incomplete plan
bodyMd:
A fictional archive held a nineteenth-century plan of a theatre. A researcher used it to reconstruct the original seating arrangement, but later found a handwritten note describing changes made during construction. The surviving plan was a proposal, not a verified record of the completed building. Photographs taken after opening showed some of the altered rows, though they did not cover the entire auditorium.

The researcher revised the reconstruction, marking well-supported elements separately from uncertain ones. The incomplete evidence did not make all reconstruction impossible. It required a distinction between what each source actually documented and what the researcher inferred. The final drawing included an explanation of these differences so that future discoveries could correct particular details without requiring readers to discard the whole study.
